note.subject: chemistry
note.title: C1–C4 school exam applications
note.overview:
## C1–C4 school exam applications (26 September 2026)

### High yield knowledge
Newlands arranged by relative atomic mass and proposed octaves, but forced dissimilar elements together and left no gaps. Mendeleev prioritised chemical properties, left gaps and sometimes changed mass order; the modern table orders by atomic number.

Choose separation methods from solubility and boiling point: filtration gives insoluble residue and liquid filtrate; evaporation leaves solute; crystallisation grows crystals after partial evaporation and cooling; simple distillation collects a solvent; fractional distillation uses a column to separate liquids with different boiling points. For salt/sugar with ethanol, dissolve sugar, filter salt residue, then remove ethanol from sugar filtrate.

RP6: pencil line 2 cm from bottom, tiny 2–3 mm spots, solvent below line, paper clear of beaker wall, mark solvent front immediately, measure start line to centre of spot and to solvent front. Rf = spot distance / solvent-front distance, no unit. One spot supports a pure sample under these conditions; overlapping substances remain possible. Compare identities only under matching solvent and conditions. Better solvent produces clearer separated spots. Ethanol is flammable.

### Marking guidance
For setup error questions pair each error with its consequence. For Rf show both distances and division. For conclusions quote spot count or positions and avoid saying matching Rf proves identity.

### Source caution
The six-page revision sheet contains a proposed “salt and sugar” example consistent with the cover lesson. The lab book’s handwritten result table is not used as a numerical answer key because its text extraction is ambiguous.

Newlands arranged by relative atomic mass and proposed octaves, but forced dissimilar elements together and left no gaps. Mendeleev prioritised chemical properties, left gaps and sometimes changed mass order; the modern table orders by atomic number.

Choose separation methods from solubility and boiling point: filtration gives insoluble residue and liquid filtrate; evaporation leaves solute; crystallisation grows crystals after partial evaporation and cooling; simple distillation collects a solvent; fractional distillation uses a column to separate liquids with different boiling points. For salt/sugar with ethanol, dissolve sugar, filter salt residue, then remove ethanol from sugar filtrate.

RP6: pencil line 2 cm from bottom, tiny 2–3 mm spots, solvent below line, paper clear of beaker wall, mark solvent front immediately, measure start line to centre of spot and to solvent front. Rf = spot distance / solvent-front distance, no unit. One spot supports a pure sample under these conditions; overlapping substances remain possible. Compare identities only under matching solvent and conditions. Better solvent produces clearer separated spots. Ethanol is flammable.

### Marking guidance
For setup error questions pair each error with its consequence. For Rf show both distances and division. For conclusions quote spot count or positions and avoid saying matching Rf proves identity.

### Source caution
The six-page revision sheet contains a proposed “salt and sugar” example consistent with the cover lesson. The lab book’s handwritten result table is not used as a numerical answer key because its text extraction is ambiguous.

note.title: Year 9 translation, verbs and Aeneas
note.overview:
## Year 9 school translation, verbs and Aeneas (26 September 2026)

### Production before recognition
Rebuild 1st and 2nd declension tables and label nominative (subject), accusative (object or after movement preposition), genitive (possession), dative (recipient), and ablative after suitable prepositions. For conjugations inspect infinitive: -are first; -ēre second; -ere third (including capio, capere third -io); -ire fourth. Present personal endings -o/-m, -s, -t, -mus, -tis, -nt; imperfect -bam etc, with changes by conjugation. Check person, tense, number and case when translating into Latin.

Possum: possum, potes, potest, possumus, potestis, possunt; imperfect poteram, poteras, poterat, poteramus, poteratis, poterant. In Trojan Horse passage, distinguish past narrative from present direct speech. For literary comprehension of The Loss of Creusa, support each answer with the supplied text: flight, discovery of Creusa’s absence at Ceres’s place, Aeneas’s search, and her ghost’s prophecy.

### Teacher-slide cautions
The teacher answer slide labels capio as “3 / 4”; specifically classify capio, capere as third conjugation -io. A translation slide mistakenly says “Trojans said” for “Graeci inquiunt”; attribution depends on the passage and should be checked rather than copied. The grammar handout contains apparent typos in example agreement and bonorun; use bonorum for masculine/neuter genitive plural of bonus. GCSE vocabulary lists are long-term reference, not evidence that every entry has been taught in current Year 9 lessons.

### Production before recognition
Rebuild 1st and 2nd declension tables and label nominative (subject), accusative (object or after movement preposition), genitive (possession), dative (recipient), and ablative after suitable prepositions. For conjugations inspect infinitive: -are first; -ēre second; -ere third (including capio, capere third -io); -ire fourth. Present personal endings -o/-m, -s, -t, -mus, -tis, -nt; imperfect -bam etc, with changes by conjugation. Check person, tense, number and case when translating into Latin.

Possum: possum, potes, potest, possumus, potestis, possunt; imperfect poteram, poteras, poterat, poteramus, poteratis, poterant. In Trojan Horse passage, distinguish past narrative from present direct speech. For literary comprehension of The Loss of Creusa, support each answer with the supplied text: flight, discovery of Creusa’s absence at Ceres’s place, Aeneas’s search, and her ghost’s prophecy.

### Teacher-slide cautions
The teacher answer slide labels capio as “3 / 4”; specifically classify capio, capere as third conjugation -io. A translation slide mistakenly says “Trojans said” for “Graeci inquiunt”; attribution depends on the passage and should be checked rather than copied. The grammar handout contains apparent typos in example agreement and bonorun; use bonorum for masculine/neuter genitive plural of bonus. GCSE vocabulary lists are long-term reference, not evidence that every entry has been taught in current Year 9 lessons.

note.overview:
## French Year 9 booklet: grammar in use (26 September 2026)

### Retrieval ladder
The Year 8 booklet explicitly advises producing spelling, pronunciation, listening recognition and sentences from memory; re-reading only tests recognition. Use English-to-French production and spaced review rather than mirrored consecutive cards.

Present regular verbs and key irregulars (avoir, être, aller, faire) underpin Unit 1 holidays, weather and next summer. Passé composé uses avoir or être plus past participle; basic subject agreement with être, e.g. elle est allée, but elle a mangé. Reflexive negatives place ne before pronoun and pas after conjugated verb: je ne me réveille pas. Write connected answers with time frame, accurate tense, opinion and reason. Childhood habits use imperfect, e.g. quand j’étais plus jeune, je jouais.

### Marking guidance
Open writing allows different truthful content. Award marks for tense, person, agreement, time phrase and reason; do not use exact sentence matching. Continue to ignore missing French accents for app practice while teaching their spelling. The Year 9 carnet covers more units than the currently taught lesson: assign future units as preview until taught.

additionalSourceSections.title: School update: active production and spacing
paragraphs: Teacher update 26 September 2026: 60 English-to-French production items now share concept IDs with the original recognition cards. Ask for spelling from memory; separate opposite directions in a session and use 2-day / 7-day review. Unit 1 is the immediate practice focus; later booklet units are preview until taught.
